title: feat: cookie consent with region-aware banner, blocker and cookie policy
body:
## What changed

Adds the cookie consent MVP that replaces Complianz:

- **Blocker** (`includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-blocker.php`): output buffer that holds back scripts and iframes from 23 known services (`includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-services.php`), plus owner-added patterns; embeds get a same-size placeholder with a Load button. Unknown third-party script hosts are recorded (up to 20) for the settings card.
- **Consent feature** (`includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php`): settings, banner and Cookie settings dialog (`includes/views/consent-banner.php`), footer menu link, button, block and shortcode, `#cookie-settings` links, Complianz one-off import.
- **Browser** (`assets/js/spcc-head.js`, `assets/js/spcc.js`): region model from the time zone (opt-in for Europe, Quebec and unclear; opt-out elsewhere; quiet option), GPC, Google Consent Mode v2, WP Consent API, release in document order, cookie removal and reload when consent is taken back. A Load button allows one service without answering the banner (`p: 1` in the cookie).
- **Cookie policy feature** (`includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-policy.php`): block and `[spcc_cookie_policy]` listing detected services' cookies; privacy policy guide text.
- **Styles** (`assets/css/spcc.css`): Kadence palette and block theme tokens, bottom bar or corner box, mobile bottom sheet, 44px targets, reduced motion.
- **Docs**: `docs/architecture.md`, README, readme.txt, changelogs, `AGENTS.md`, `DESIGN.md` → Front end; uninstall removes the seen list.

## Why

Complianz needs a scan, a wizard and upkeep. This works when switched on, keeps the HTML the same for every visitor (page caches), and asks only as strictly as each region needs. Defaults are configurable and not legal advice.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all stages pass (PHP, JS, shell, workflows, PHPCS, PHPStan).
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (WordPress 7.1.3, PHP 8.3) and `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`: pass, no PHP messages, both features on. The seen list is autoloaded from the first page, so no per-page lookup.
- Playwright on a test site with GA, Meta Pixel, YouTube and Google Maps:
  - Europe/London: banner names all four services; nothing loads; Consent Mode default denied; dialog rows by category; Escape closes; Load video loads YouTube only and the banner stays (also after reload); Reject all then reloads and removes it.
  - Europe/Berlin: Accept all loads everything; Reject all from Cookie settings reloads and stops it.
  - Europe/Paris: Statistics only loads GA alone.
  - America/New_York: loads with a short notice; America/Chicago with GPC: marketing off.
  - Tab order: banner before the skip link; no JS errors in any scenario.
  - Mobile and simulated Kadence dark palette screenshots reviewed.
- Admin: Consent card lists found services by category and unknown hosts; region labels fit the select.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: 0 errors. Warnings left are release-time items (Unreleased changelog sections, the WordPress.org slug note, the starter's banner, icon and screenshots) and one false positive: `.spcc-panel-note` is the documented panel wrapper (`admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php`), which the core class-name check does not recognise.
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: no errors on either zip (GitHub zip: only the expected updater findings). Library CDNs were dropped from the "not worth listing" hosts, since they still receive visitors' IP addresses; the security hosts kept there (reCAPTCHA, Turnstile) carry a `phpcs:ignore` with the reason.

GitHub Actions did not start on this PR: the account's Actions billing reports failed payments or a spending limit. The local runs above cover the same jobs (lint, smoke test on 7.1/PHP 8.3 and 6.2/PHP 7.4, release build, preflight, Plugin Check).

Not in this PR (follow-ups): screenshots and banner art for WordPress.org, Scan now button and first-run guide, lightbox embeds added after page load.

Resolves #2

title: GH#17: banner above floating bars, theme-proof button states, optional floating settings button
body:
Resolves #17

## Changes

- **Banner layer:** `.spcc-banner` uses `z-index: var(--spcc-z, 2147483000)`, above TranslatePress's floating switcher (`9999999`) and typical chat buttons. The non-modal dialog fallback sits one above and the floating button one below. Sites can override `--spcc-z` on `:root`.
- **Theme-proof button states:** Kadence styles every `button:hover/:focus/:active` (white text, theme background, shadow). The dialog's × now sets its colour on hover, focus and active. The quiet Settings button, Load buttons, embed Cookie settings link and floating button do the same.
- **Floating button optional, off by default:** new `consent_floating_button` setting (Options → Floating Cookie settings button). `footer()` prints `.spcc-reopen` only when it is on and no menu link or block button was printed. `spcc.js` already handles a missing button.
- Docs: `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`.

No migration: unreleased.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- Kadence's rule confirmed in `themes/kadence/assets/css/global.min.css` (`button:hover,button:focus,button:active{color:var(--global-palette-btn-hover);background:var(--global-palette-btn-bg-hover);box-shadow:…}`).
- Browser check on the preview site: see the follow-up comment.

title: GH#19: settings banner preview, Cookie policy page picker, block settings
body:
Resolves #19

## Changes

- **Banner preview** (Consent card, closed by default, open state remembered): the home page in a frame with `?spcc_preview=opt-in|opt-out`, sized for desktop (1280px) or phone (390px). It reloads after each `consent*` setting saves. Preview mode applies only to `manage_options` users. It ignores the stored choice and never releases, saves or signals consent. Links don't navigate and the toolbar is hidden.
- **Cookie policy page picker:** jQuery UI autocomplete (core) over `/wp/v2/search` pages on `#spcc-consent_policy_url`. It saves a home-relative path; typed addresses still work.
- **Block settings:** `SEOProCookieConsent_Setup::register_block()` takes `attributes`; `assets/js/blocks.js` renders `InspectorControls` (Toggle, Select, Text) and passes attributes to `ServerSideRender`.
  - Cookie policy: introduction, Cookie settings button, last-updated date, heading level.
  - Cookie settings: text, and button or link.
  - The shortcodes take the same options.
- No starter core files changed (`scripts/core-files.txt`): only plugin-owned hooks (`seoprocookieconsent_setting_panel`, `seoprocookieconsent_admin_enqueue`) and plugin files.
- Docs: `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `docs/architecture.md`.

## Verification

title: GH#7: hold back dynamically inserted scripts and iframes
body:
## Summary

Resolves #7.

- Guard dynamic script/iframe sources and common DOM insertions before requests start; observe added nodes for placeholders.
- Reuse the existing consent choice, banner, dialog and release paths.
- Preserve exclusions, Google advanced mode and editor bypasses.

Adds compact URL match fragments from the existing service list (retaining paths on shared hosts), translated placeholder copy, settings exclusions and editor-bypass activation. No per-view reporting or visitor-dependent HTML.

Dynamic-only limitations are documented: inline-only injected code, shadow roots, other documents, `document.write`/range APIs, `srcdoc`, fetch/XHR and saved native methods require integrations to consult consent. Optimizers must not delay the consent head script. No legal or region defaults change.

## Runtime Testing

- Risk: medium.
- Level: runtime-verified, head `7bd6aa6451856400945d36545cbf6c76128997cd`.
- `scripts/lint.sh`: PHP/JS syntax, ShellCheck, actionlint, PHPCS and PHPStan pass; no JS build is configured. The final URL-filter tweak also passed scoped PHP syntax/PHPCS and final browser rerun.
- Isolated WordPress 7.1.3 / PHP 8.3, headless Brave, Europe/London: dynamic YouTube iframe and GA script make **zero requests before consent**. Load releases YouTube only; Accept releases GA exactly once. Reject never loads either.
- Verified appendChild, append/prepend, nested DocumentFragment, replaceChild, live innerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML and connected iframe src/property or setAttribute changes. Placeholders and the banner appear on a previously empty page; it stays hidden without matches.
- Verified original script `onload` and addEventListener callbacks fire once; changed held URLs release only the latest source; unmatched and empty sources discard stale blocking metadata/wrappers. Opt-out discovers an allowed service for the notice; ignored/JSON scripts retain their behavior. Actual settings for Never hold back and Google advanced mode permit the excluded services.
- No browser pageerrors; WordPress debug log empty. Disposable site removed and preview-browser session logged out.
- Nine-sample no-match insertion probe: median **0.5 ms** for 1,000 insertions with dynamic guards versus **0.4 ms** without; banner stayed hidden. This bounded microbenchmark is not a whole-site performance guarantee.

## Acceptance and review

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Dynamically inserted script/iframe held before requests | Zero-request browser checks above |
| Placeholder and consent release use existing UI | Load/Reject/Accept and callback checks above |
| No JS errors; negligible no-match work | Empty pageerror list and insertion comparison |
| Config remains compact and page-cache safe | Shared URL fragments only; server activation flag, no per-visitor HTML |
| Required lint | All configured lint checks passed |

Independent read-only review identified stale-source state and discarded loader callbacks; both were fixed and browser-verified. Its follow-up identified empty-source cancellation; that too was fixed and verified. Remaining changes received direct diff/acceptance review. Review bundle SHA-256: `28e614d0e49da0eb9432c2e28cbfb66df42d6fff680076b5280f458ed204ba8c`.

## External/pre-existing observations

- CI run [38846566468](https://github.com/wpallstars/seoprocookieconsent/actions/runs/38846566468/job/116798334111) failed before actionlint could execute: Docker Hub returned **429 Too Many Requests** fetching unchanged `rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12` (exit 125). This is an external registry rate limit, not a change-caused lint finding; local actionlint and full lint pass. Ready-state CI is queued. No workflow/image changes or rerun polling are made in this task.
- Qlty reports **“Qlty did not run because you are out of minutes.”** This is provider quota, not a code finding; no check or protection was weakened.
- The existing shared site's optimizer rewrites the consent head script to `seoprostack/delayed` for anonymous visitors; authenticated preview and the isolated WordPress runtime were used rather than changing another plugin. Optimizer exclusions are documented.
- Shared preview includes PR #22 but currently skips this PR due to conflicting documentation changes. Isolated runtime verification uses this PR's exact implementation, not the combined preview. Preview merge conflicts do not affect this PR's clean merge against its current base.
